qupXap5BBOE.title: STABILIZERS in MEAD Making at Home: Mistake?
qupXap5BBOE.creator: City Steading Brews
qupXap5BBOE.description:
Ever wondered whether chemical stabilization changes the flavor of mead? We finally put it to the test!

In this experiment we brewed one traditional mead and divided it into three versions:
•A control
•A chemically stabilized mead (potassium metabisulfite & potassium sorbate)
•A pasteurized mead

Each sample was back sweetened with the same honey and then tasted side-by-side to find out if there is a noticeable difference in aroma and flavor.

Our Strawberry Rhubarb Mead that inspired this test: https://youtu.be/Bddy9HFbe4I?si=zlA7K2zmZe87cw9F
How We Rack a Brew: https://youtu.be/-X00d3C14z0?si=U0zhkWSyLWHpmqZ3

City Steading Merchandise: https://briancity-steadingcom-1-shop.fourthwall.com/
Tools We Use: 
1.5 US Gallon Fermenter: https://amzn.to/4vb6oGg
Digital Scale: https://amzn.to/4dxaqkr
Our Favorite Pitcher: https://amzn.to/4dFWNzh
Star San: https://amzn.to/3SXFoKg
TRBOS: https://amzn.to/3WROzxD
Spaddle: https://amzn.to/4bM43IQ
Paddle & Spoon Set: https://amzn.to/44HDpz3
Baster: https://amzn.to/3DXs2c8
Graduated Cylinder & Hydrometer: https://amzn.to/4ow8gXz
Tilt Digital Hydrometer: https://amzn.to/4njWPkv
Auto Siphon: https://amzn.to/4cz8VRr
SOL: https://amzn.to/4w8LSrB
Anova Culinary Sous Vide Precision Cooker: https://amzn.to/40fWdmV
Glencairn Glasses: https://amzn.to/3Fbll78
We use the Amazon Affiliate Program for these links and we DO receive a small commission if you purchase using our links and all this comes at no additional cost to you!
_____________________________________
This isn't a debate based on opinions—it's a practical brewing experiment designed to help home mead makers decide which stabilization method works best for them.

If you've ever asked:
• Does potassium sorbate affect flavor?
• Does Campden change the taste of mead?
• Is pasteurization better than chemical stabilization?
• Which stabilization method should I use?

...this video is for you.

Ingredients (Base Mead)
2 lbs honey
Water (to 1 gallon)
Premier Classique wine yeast: https://amzn.to/4h7wCGt
Honey for back sweetening (equal amount added to each sample)
Chemical Stabilization
Potassium Metabisulfite (Campden): https://amzn.to/4yRXEbh
Potassium Sorbate: https://amzn.to/4umICrd
Pasteurization
Heated to 140°F (60°C) for 22 minutes

We hope this comparison helps you decide which stabilization method best fits your own brewing style.

Have you compared pasteurized and chemically stabilized mead? Let us know your results in the comments!

Today we attempted something a little different…
A sweet, naturally carbonated mead using raw honey from a small farm. The goal was simple:
   🍯 Sweet

We use the Amazon Affiliate Program for these links and we DO receive a small commission if you purchase using our links and all this comes at no additional cost to you!

In this video we walk through the full process of making sparkling mead, including:

• Starting a traditional honey wine
• Calculating gravity and ABV
• Naturally carbonating (bottle conditioning)
• Using non-fermentable sweeteners
• Troubleshooting carbonation issues

And when it’s finally time to open the bottles… things get interesting.
   *Was it the weather?
   *Was it the sweetener?
   *Did the carbonation fail?
Even when a brew doesn’t come out exactly as planned, there’s always something to learn.

That’s part of the fun of home brewing.
_____________________________________
🍯 Ingredients
[Primary Fermentation]
   *3 lb (1.36 kg) raw honey (Adee Farms honey)

   *½ packet Mangrove Jack's M02 Cider Yeast: https://amzn.to/4be7qcM
   *½ tsp Fermaid O: https://amzn.to/4cw6sb4

Starting Gravity: ~1.104

[Sweetening (Post Fermentation)]
   *Allulose (added to taste): https://amzn.to/4rRhVJY

[Bottle Conditioning (Carbonation)]
   *42 g (1.5 oz) sugar for priming
   *A few grains Lalvin EC‑1118 as insurance yeast

uPur05swq2U.title: OFFENSIVE Mead? - Step Feed Pyment Mead Recipe
uPur05swq2U.creator: City Steading Brews
uPur05swq2U.description:
Why is this offensive mead?  Well, it might not be a mead!  It's certainly fermented grape juice, and there's fermented honey too, but... does that make it a MEAD?  Or is it a honey flavored wine?  Anyway, it's a pyment (if you consider it a mead), which is grape and honey fermented together.  So, if you see it as a mead, it's a pyment, if you don't see it as a mead, it's wine.  See?  Offensive to a lot of brewers, lol.

MoBq0QayjPY.title: This Mead Looked Disgusting... then THIS Happened: Apple Butter Mead
MoBq0QayjPY.creator: City Steading Brews
MoBq0QayjPY.description:
Can you make mead with apple butter?
Well... yes. But we're not sure we'd recommend it. 😂
Someone suggested that we try making a mead using apple butter, and it sounded just strange enough that we had to find out what would happen.
We started with three jars of apple butter made from apples, sugar and spices, added some fantastic wildflower honey from our friend Dave's own apiary, and fermented the whole thing with Mangrove Jack's M05 Mead Yeast.
Technically, that makes this a cyser—a mead made with apples and honey—but using concentrated, cooked-down apple butter gives this one a character all its own.

It also creates a LOT of apple goop.

Apple Butter Mead Recipe
3 × 17 oz jars apple butter: https://link.amazon/B07Zgzqeq
2 lbs wildflower honey (thanks Dave!)
100 fl oz water
½ packet Mangrove Jack's M05 Mead Yeast: https://link.amazon/B0h5jmA0M
1 Amburana wood stick for aging: https://barrelcharwood.com/
Additional honey for backsweetening

Starting Gravity: 1.106
Final Gravity: 0.996
Approximate ABV: 14%
Gravity after backsweetening: 1.024

City Steading Merchandise: https://briancity-steadingcom-1-shop.fourthwall.com/
Tools We Use: 
1.5 US Gallon Fermenter: https://amzn.to/47LOkdX
Scale: https://amzn.to/4dxaqkr
Star San: https://amzn.to/3SXFoKg
Our Favorite Pitcher: https://amzn.to/4dFWNzh
Paddle: https://amzn.to/44HDpz3
Graduated Cylinder and Hydrometer: https://amzn.to/4ow8gXz
SOL: https://amzn.to/4w8LSrB
Auto Siphon: https://amzn.to/4cz8VRr
Fine Mesh Brew Bag: https://amzn.to/4nCuVk4
1 US Gallon Wide Mouth Fermenter: https://amzn.to/43TNwS2
Mini Mason Jar Mugs: https://amzn.to/3S0QzUK
Stainless Steel Milk Jug: https://amzn.to/3QNC8mw
Belgian Tasting Glasses: https://amzn.to/3Zg67Wr
We use the Amazon Affiliate Program for these links and we DO receive a small commission if you purchase using our links and all this comes at no additional cost to you!

How We Pasteurize: https://youtu.be/zWBU3EI-EFo?si=siPEDmpR7Seai6WK
Hive and Harvest Mead Recipe: https://youtu.be/DC32O_AKk_U?si=EGWePdsCf1BbCwHU

The fermentation itself wasn't the problem. Getting the finished mead separated from all that apple sediment was another story.

The final verdict?

Yes, you absolutely CAN make a delicious mead from apple butter. It's rich, mouth-filling and reminds us of fall and the holidays.

But there's a catch: It's kind of a pain in the butt.

If you just want a spiced cyser, apple juice and spices would be considerably easier. But if you happen to have a bunch of apple butter sitting around—or just enjoy making weird brews like we do—this one definitely works.

Sometimes you make a brew because it's the easiest way to make something delicious.
Sometimes you make it just to find out if you can.

Have Questions? Ask in the comments section and we will get back to you ASAP.
Thanks for watching!
